summary.headline: Seshaasai Q2 FY27 revenue rose 15% YoY to Rs 4,053.1 mn, with PAT up 21% YoY to Rs 697.3 mn and gross margin at 42.5%.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 15% YoY and 7.7% QoQ, led by Payment Solutions, which rose 21.7% YoY and 38% QoQ. Gross margin recovered 89 bps QoQ to 42.5% on mix and operating leverage, but remained 331 bps lower YoY because of a weaker rupee and higher input and logistics costs. EBITDA margin was 26.3% and finance costs fell 74.9% YoY after debt repayment. Management said H2 should again be better than H1, and that Q3 margins may better reflect current input costs.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 2,009.7 mn (25.7% margin) / Rs 1,300.7 mn (16.6% margin)
Rs 3,144 mn; net cash about Rs 2,407 mn

segments.name: Payment Solutions
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 2,182.6 mn, +21.7% YoY and +38% QoQ, driven by debit cards, mass transit programmes, metal cards and exports. Export revenue is about 5% of H1 payment card business.

segments.name: Communication and Fulfillment Solutions
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 1,290.1 mn, broadly flat YoY and down QoQ as Q1 and Q4 carry larger volumes and yearly one-time projects. Renewed 3-year contracts with a PSU bank and a PSU life insurer.

segments.name: IoT Solutions
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 551.9 mn, +45.6% YoY but down QoQ after a large retail customer tagging migration in Q1. H1 IoT growth about 45.8% YoY; FY27 target is about 45% growth over FY26 IoT revenue.

guidance_outlook: H2 expected to be better than H1, supported by card volumes, premium and metal cards, the mass transit programme and IoT ramp-up.
FY27 IoT revenue target of about 45% YoY growth over FY26.
Q3 may better reflect current input costs; management said Q2 should not be far from normalised rupee levels.
eSIM revenue not in this year's plan; management hopes to begin something by the turn of the year and expects good prospects next financial year.
SIM card line expected at about 70-75% capacity utilisation in the current and next month.
capex_capacity: New metal card facility being set up, operational soon, with 3x current metal card capacity.

Cumulative IPO fund utilisation Rs 4,803.9 mn, incl. Rs 849.2 mn capex, Rs 3,000 mn debt repayment, Rs 343.7 mn issue expenses and Rs 611 mn general corporate purposes; unutilised proceeds about Rs 1,196.1 mn.
Continuing investment in infrastructure and equipment across verticals, balanced against cash flow and working capital.
Product qualification under way for SIM card supplies to another large telecom operator; eSIM qualification with one telco expected to finish in about six months.
demand_pricing: Some customer contracts are passing through input price hikes; others up for renewal are being repriced in revised proposals.
Management described USD-INR, fuel and petrochemical input costs as outside its control and said material costs rose faster than revenue YoY.
Inventory was built up ahead of Q3 because of high semiconductor lead times and holiday supply-chain risk, and for new SIM variants.
Export push to Europe and Africa through personalisation bureaus and system integrators, focused on premium plastic cards; metal card exports are at sampling and qualification stage.
RFID pilots in eyewear, FMCG and pharma; revenue already begun in eye care and non-renewable segments.

qa_highlights.question: Which card types drove Payment Solutions growth, and what is the export business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited mass transit programmes and debit cards as main drivers, plus metal cards and exports to Europe and Africa that began in Q1 and picked up in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How should the IoT segment be tracked, QoQ or YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 FY27 IoT grew about 45.8% YoY, with Q1 seasonally high from retail festive preparation and a one-time tagging migration, and expects FY27 growth of about 45%.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 again be stronger than H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management expects H2 to be better, with Q1 FY26 having been weak, which amplified last year's H1-H2 gap.

qa_highlights.question: Are input cost increases being passed on, and when do they ease?
qa_highlights.answer: Some customers accepted price hikes; contracts up for renewal are being repriced. Management said input costs are largely outside its control and is focusing on product mix and lean operations.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company affected by the UPI MDR change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said possible MDR on UPI would reduce the incentive gap between UPI and cards, which it sees as favourable for the business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export share and how large is the metal card opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are about 5% of H1 payment card business. Metal card exports are in sampling and qualification, with a new facility at 3x current metal capacity coming soon.

qa_highlights.question: Does Q2 margin reflect spot input costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory consumed in Q2 was largely at normalised rupee levels, so Q2 should be close to normal, and Q3 may better reflect current costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory build up, and what is SIM utilisation and eSIM timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory was built for Q3 demand, semiconductor lead times and new SIM variants. SIM utilisation is 70-75%; eSIM qualification with one telco should finish in about six months, with no eSIM revenue planned this year.

risks_watch: Gross margin remains 331 bps lower YoY; further input cost pressure from USD-INR, fuel and semiconductors could reach Q3.
Inventory build-up for semiconductor supply and new SIM variants adds working capital and obsolescence risk.
IoT revenue fell QoQ; sustaining the 45% FY27 growth target depends on SIM onboarding and retail seasonality.
eSIM and SIM revenue depend on lengthy telco qualification cycles.
Mass transit programme is described as one-off; its durability is a question for next quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, margin recovery and H2 outlook, but cautious on input costs and the rupee, which management called outside its control. It declined to split out mass transit revenue and gave no firm timeline for eSIM revenue.
key_quotes: Sequential revenue growth with a better product mix outpaced the increase in material cost, driving an 89 bps improvement in gross margin to 42.5%.
So, I would say that we continue to maintain the expectation that H2 would be better than H1.
So, to my mind, inventories which have been consumed in Q2, or the input costs in Q2, pretty much to a great extent almost are at the normalized level of the rupee at this stage.
